arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Millett argued the Fifth Circuit had the power to hear the appeal but decided the case wrongly.
Mr. Mitchell argued the Fifth Circuit lacked power because the certificate failed to meet legal requirements.
Mr. Delaney argued the certificate must name a specific constitutional claim to be valid.
Justice Scalia questioned whether the certificate's failure to name an issue invalidates it entirely.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the rules for appealing a federal habeas corpus decision. A habeas petition asks a judge to release a prisoner if their detention violates the law. To appeal a denial, a prisoner must get a certificate of appealability. The core question is whether this certificate must list a specific legal claim to be valid.

Thaler argues the certificate was invalid because the law requires it to identify a specific constitutional claim to grant appeal power.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the minimum requirements for a prisoner to appeal a habeas denial. It determines whether a vague certificate allows courts to review legal errors. The outcome shapes the procedural path for all federal prisoners seeking appellate review of their detention.
